transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-21
Start: 15:00 PT - Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Sam Patel (Redwood SE), Taylor Nguyen (Redwood Product), Maya Rodriguez (Atlas Dir. of Data), Ethan Brooks (Atlas SRE), Priya Singh (Atlas Security Lead)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focussing on tracing, error analysis, request logs and how to debug production incidents.
Links shared: Deck: https://redwood.ai/share/atlas-health/console-deck | Benchmark: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/atlas-request-logs.xlsx | Security: https://redwood.ai/security/atlas-soc2.pdf

00:00 Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna take you through the console tracing and request logs today, um - quick agenda, tracer overview, error analysis, then a live debugging flow, sound good?
00:12 Maya: yeah great, thanks, we've been seeing some 95th percentile latency spikes on inference, want to understand root cause and how Redwood helps debug those
00:22 Avery: perfect, Sam will drive the console demo, I'll chime on product/pricing and Taylor on rollout/observability bits
00:35 Sam: alright sharing screen now - tell me if the screen is fuzzy, sometimes the auto-transcript messes up names so ignore that
01:05 Sam: (screen) this is the Console Traces view, you can see traces aggregated by route, model, and region. note the sampling toggles here - by default we do adaptive sampling to keep payload small
01:30 Ethan: quick q - do you store full request logs by default or is that opt-in? we need retention for 90 days for a subset of customers
01:45 Sam: good q - hosted stores summarized traces by default, full raw request logs are opt-in via request-logs export and can be routed to your S3 or GCS with our kms-integration, retention configurable up to 365 days for enterprise
02:10 Priya: is that encrypted with our KMS? we need to ensure customer-managed keys
02:22 Sam: yes, we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key). the export path uses envelope encryption and we log key usage. I'll link the KMS notes after the call
02:40 Avery: also note we have VPC/private deployment options if needed for stricter network controls
03:05 Sam: back to the traces, here's an example trace for a high-latency request - you'll see spans for auth, routing, model inference, kv-cache hit/miss etc. sometimes the transcriber renders kv-cache as 'k v cash' so ignore weirdness
03:28 Maya: can you show the error analysis flow - like how we'd find a root cause across traces and request logs?
03:40 Sam: yeah, so first we filter to the failing route, then isolate by model and timeframe, then jump to the request log for that trace - I'll pull one where the 95p jumps
04:10 Sam: (clicks) here you can see an error burst correlated with a specific model version and a particular backend pod. notice the flame chart, it shows repeated requeueing which increases latency
04:35 Ethan: requeueing due to OOM on the pod? or a networking socket timeout?
04:45 Sam: from the trace metadata it's a context deadline exceeded in the infer node - could be GPU contention or kernel fallback. we then pull the request logs to see payload size and batching info
05:10 Sam: (opens request log) raw request log shows prompt size, token count, batching group, model variant and kernel flags. here's an example where a client sent a burst of long prompts causing the batch to skew and raise latency
05:40 Maya: ah, that matches our spike pattern - lots of long customer messages at 3am PST when the ML-heavy jobs run
06:00 Sam: right, and Console lets you visualize batch composition over time so you can see average seq length and batch latency. we also provide automated suggestions for batching config and quantization to reduce p99
06:28 Taylor: and we can surface model recommendations based on your workload profile - e.g., switch to a lower-latency quantized variant for high-throughput routes with tolerant quality requirements
06:50 Priya: curious - what tracing retention and access controls do you have? we need role-based access, audit logs and SSO w/ SAML
07:05 Avery: we map RBAC to SAML groups, audit logs are exportable to your SIEM, and every action in the Console is logged with actor and timestamp. SOC2 and ISO docs are in the security pack I'll share
07:30 Sam: back to debugging - another useful view is Request Timeline which lines up traces, errors, and infra metrics. you can jump from a trace to the exact container logs or to the matching request log stored in S3
08:00 Ethan: does the request log include the full input text? privacy wise we might need redaction or retention controls
08:15 Sam: configured per-export: you can redact inputs at export time or only export metadata (prompt length, tokens, model). for regulated users we also support tokenization or on-prem export
08:35 Maya: for the POC we'd want raw logs but redacted for PHI fields - is there an auto-redact option?
08:45 Sam: yes we have a json-path based redact config, and we can run an initial pass during export to mask patterns. again I'll attach docs and an example config
09:10 Sam: jumping to Error Analysis panel - it clusters errors by type, model, and route. you can click an error cluster and get drilldowns into top traces and sample request logs
09:40 Maya: show us an example where the cluster helped narrow to a model bug
09:50 Sam: here's one - error cluster shows higher latency for a specific quantized kernel on one GPU family. we correlated kernel selection logs with the model rollout and discovered the new quant config pushed a fallback path for certain token lengths
10:20 Taylor: that's a good example for rollout policies - you can pin model versions for a percentage of traffic, and have automatic fallback to a stable variant when error rate or p95 exceed thresholds
10:45 Ethan: during the spike, can we replay requests to a safety sandbox to reproduce? we want to run a local repro before changing production
11:00 Sam: yes, Console supports request replay against a dedicated sandbox or local dev endpoint; you can replay using the exact payload and headers. note that replays are throttled to avoid accidental load
11:20 Maya: ok what about instrumentation - how lightweight is the tracing? we run on edge gateways and want minimal perf hit
11:35 Sam: tracing is designed to be low overhead: span context is small, sampling is adaptive and you can disable detailed KV cache spans on high-throughput routes. our tests show <1% overhead for typical web workloads
11:55 Priya: another security question - do you keep request payloads in Redwood logs longer than customer retention? we need guaranteed deletion on contract termination
12:08 Avery: Deletion requests are supported with a documented wipe process and we issue certificates of deletion for enterprise contracts. that's in the security pack as well
12:30 Sam: now I'll demo a live debugging flow end-to-end: find the spike, identify requeueing, check batch skew, pull request logs, and set a canary rollback rule
13:05 Sam: (narrating) filter traces 2/10/2028 02:30-03:30, route: /inference/order, model: rdx-13b-quant-v2, p95 jumped to 1.8s. click a sample trace - span shows 'batch_wakeup' waiting 420ms
13:40 Ethan: is there an ETA for improving batch wakeup heuristics? that's been a thorn for us
13:50 Taylor: we actually have an Optimize rule engine that suggests batching policy tweaks based on historical seq length and traffic shape; we can run that against your logs and propose settings
14:12 Maya: would that require onboarded logs first? we can upload a week's worth for the POC
14:25 Sam: you can either connect live streaming or upload historical logs, both work. for analysis we prefer sample week of raw request logs plus a short trace dump
14:50 Priya: how do we control who can export raw logs? we have strict separation, ops can export but product can't
15:00 Avery: RBAC supports export permissions scoped to teams and specific buckets; exports require a signed request and we log the actor
15:20 Maya: can you show the request-log schema briefly so our SRE can map fields?
15:30 Sam: sure, sample log has timestamp, request_id, route, model_variant, prompt_length, token_count, batch_id, kernel_flags, latency_ms, error_code, user_id (if provided), and full_input optionally. again I'll attach the schema and the example CSV
16:00 Sam: (shows) here you can also run queries on logs in the Console with a SQL-ish interface to pivot by batch_id or token_count
16:20 Ethan: good - we'll want to filter by batch_id to find correlated high-latency requests
16:30 Sam: exactly. also Console ties infra metrics to traces (GPU utilization, memory) so you can see if high p95 coincides with GPU swap or OOMs
16:50 Maya: we saw one trace where kernel fallback occurred which increased CPU usage. can you flag kernel fallbacks as an alert?
17:05 Sam: yes you can set a trace-based alert rule; when kernel_fallback_count > 0 for 5m then page the oncall, and optionally trigger a Canary rollback
17:25 Priya: for audit we need change history on alert thresholds too - is that stored?
17:35 Avery: yes changes are in audit logs with actor, timestamp, and diff. retention configurable per plan
17:50 Sam: small note - transcripts sometimes mislabel spans; the Console trace metadata is the source of truth, not the transcript language, so check trace fields for exact kernel names
18:10 Maya: are there templates for SOC2 evidence collection tied to tracing? like we need to show PRs and config changes across the POC
18:25 Avery: we have a compliance kit which maps Console artifacts to control evidence; will include checklist and sample exports for the POC
18:40 Sam: demo follow-up - I'll drop in a sample request log and a trace that reproduces your p95 spike to the shared spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/atlas-request-logs.xlsx
19:05 Maya: thanks. what about Dedicated capacity - if we move to dedicated GPUs will the tracing change? we want the same Console UX but private network
19:20 Taylor: Console and tracing are consistent across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. with Dedicated you get isolated pools and predictable throughput; traces still flow to your private control plane if you choose private deployment
19:40 Ethan: is there an extra agent to install in our VPC for private? we want minimal ops
19:50 Sam: for Private we deploy a small collector in your VPC that forwards traces and metrics to your private control plane. it's lightweight and supports mTLS and mutual auth
20:10 Priya: anything special about data residency for EU? our customers there need logs kept in EU only
20:25 Avery: we support regional retention and data residency controls; can pin exports to EU buckets and restrict routing policy by region
20:40 Maya: ok let's talk POC scope - we want to run a 4-week pilot, ingest 1 week of historical logs, connect live for 2 weeks, then run targeted replay and optimize batching. success criteria: reduce p95 by 30% and have reproducible debug workflow
21:05 Avery: 4-week pilot sounds good, we'll propose a plan and a pricing estimate. question on success metrics - will you provide a baseline p95 and traffic pattern?
21:20 Maya: we'll send baseline metrics and 3 example incidents. also need SSO + export perms set up before ingesting logs
21:35 Avery: noted. Sam - can you run a quick checklist of what you need from Atlas to start the POC?
21:45 Sam: sure - (1) one week of anonymized request logs (CSV or JSON) (2) service account for export to s3/gcs with sample bucket info (3) SAML metadata for SSO config (4) list of routes to focus on (we'll give a template)
22:20 Maya: timeline - can you get pricing and security docs by Friday? that's 2028-02-24 for us to review with procurement
22:32 Avery: yes will do. Sam will attach benchmark spreadsheet and sample logs, and I'll send security pack and dedicated pricing
22:45 Priya: last q - can we redact PII before logs hit Redwood? we prefer client-side redaction
22:55 Sam: absolutely, you can do client-side redaction and only export masked fields; Console will index the masked logs for tracing correlation but not store raw PII unless you opt-in
23:10 Maya: perfect. thanks all. one more thing - is there an SDK for automated rule creation? we'd like infra to auto-create alerts when deploys happen
23:25 Taylor: we have an APIs+SDKs for CRUD on alerts and rollouts, will share examples in the repo.
23:40 Avery: ok let's recap next steps - I'll list 'security pack', 'pricing for Dedicated', 'sample logs & trace example', and schedule POC kickoff for week of Mar 4th
24:05 Maya: that works for us - thanks Sam and Avery, demo was super helpful
24:18 Sam: thanks, we'll follow up with assets
